title: Chapter XL

teacherSummary.text: Elizabeth tells Jane of Darcy's proposal and of Wickham's true character. Jane is distressed for both men. The sisters agree not to expose Wickham publicly, since he is leaving soon. Elizabeth keeps back Darcy's part in separating Jane and Bingley.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “There certainly was some great mismanagement in the education of those two young men” slowly and put it in my own words: Elizabeth tells Jane that there must have been some great mismanagement in the education of Darcy and Wickham. Next, craft. I notice her wry, balanced judgment, now that she knows the truth from Darcy's letter. The strongest word is “mismanagement”: it means bad handling, suggesting their upbringing went wrong somehow. Then, effect. What does Elizabeth mean about the two young men's education? My answer: By the two young men's education, Elizabeth means Darcy and Wickham were badly managed: one got all the goodness and the other all the appearance of it, and she admits her misjudgment of both.

collegeSophomore.note: Use the extensions: genre and period conventions, and a published critic.

collegeJunior.note: Use the extensions: name a critical method and test it against the passage.

collegeSenior.note: Use the extensions: connect the chapter to the whole work and the scholarship.

graduate.note: Use the extensions: position answers in a critical conversation and the textual history.
